Xendit is the financial technology platform built for businesses that move fast. We give companies one unified platform for payment acceptance, payouts, treasury and financial services, replacing fragmented local integrations with a single infrastructure layer. We serve businesses of every size, from high-growth startups to global enterprises, processing high-volume transactions across Southeast Asia and beyond, with more markets on our global expansion roadmap.

Why this role exists

Designing for developers is a distinct craft. The interface is often the dashboard, the API reference, the sandbox, the error states, and the logs, information-dense surfaces for a technical audience with little patience for friction. This role makes the developer's experience clear, fast, and trustworthy across those surfaces.

What you'll own

• Product design for the developer dashboard and integration surfaces.
• Information design for docs and API reference, in partnership with Engineering and content.
• Error states, empty states, sandbox and testing flows, the moments where developers get stuck.
• Discovery with developers, and close collaboration with the DevEx PM and Engineering.

How you will work

You report to the Product Design & UX Director for Customer Lifecycle and are embedded with the Developer Experience PM and Engineering as the design owner for developer-facing surfaces. You adopt and extend the domain design system rather than owning it, partnering with the senior design-system lead on shared patterns, so your time is weighted toward product work from the start. The domain works from validated findings rather than assumptions and values direct, candid critique.

What we're looking for

• Product-design craft with evidence of designing for technical, developer, or data-dense products. A portfolio is a must.
• Comfort with information-dense UI, dashboards, tables, complex states.
• The ability to partner closely with engineers. You work well alongside technical teams.

A strong plus: having designed docs, API reference, or developer tools; technical literacy; fintech experience.
